questions.q:
India holds the chair of BRICS for 2026 and will host the summit in New Delhi. Consider the following statements:
1. India's 2026 BRICS chairmanship was backed by the UAE in the India-UAE joint statement of 19 January 2026.
2. The BRICS chairship rotates annually among the members.
3. The RBI proposed that the 2026 summit adopt a common BRICS currency to replace the US dollar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The RBI's actual proposal was narrower: put the linking of BRICS central bank digital currencies, that is interoperable payment systems, on the summit agenda; a common currency was not proposed. The idea builds on a 2025 BRICS declaration in Rio de Janeiro on payment-system interoperability.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, 22 Jan 2026; Physics Wallah monthly current affairs

questions.q:
Indian diplomat D.B. Venkatesh Varma was nominated Chair of the UN Advisory Board on Disarmament Matters for 2026-27. Consider the following statements:
1. He is the first Indian to chair the Board.
2. The Board was established in 1978.
3. Its 15 members are chosen by the UN General Assembly.
4. It also acts as the Board of Trustees of UNIDIR.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The 15 members are chosen by the UN Secretary-General, who nominates the chair, not by the General Assembly. The Board meets twice a year in New York and Geneva, and the chair rotates by region annually.

questions.q: India took part for the first time in an engagement with the Weimar Triangle in January 2026. Which one of the following lists its member countries?
o: Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic
France, Poland and the United Kingdom
questions.e: The Weimar Triangle was formed on 29 August 1991 at Weimar, Germany, to anchor German-Polish reconciliation after the Cold War; Poland joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004. It has no institutional structure, working only as a consultation forum of foreign ministers.

questions.q:
India rejected China's infrastructure activity in the Shaksgam Valley as illegal and invalid in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The valley lies south of the Siachen Glacier and is administered by India as part of Ladakh.
2. Pakistan ceded it to China under the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement, which India does not recognise.
3. China is building CPEC-linked infrastructure in the area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Shaksgam Valley (Trans-Karakoram Tract) lies north of the Siachen Glacier and is under Chinese control after the 1963 agreement, which India rejects because Pakistan had no legal title to cede territory that is part of Jammu and Kashmir. India has reaffirmed that the valley is an integral part of India.

questions.q: Pax Silica, in the news in January 2026 when the US Ambassador said India would be invited to join, is
o: An Indo-Pacific maritime security arrangement launched by India at the East Asia Summit in 2019
A BRICS payment system for settling trade in local currencies
A Quad initiative on laying undersea cables
A US-led coalition on silicon, AI and critical-minerals supply chains whose inaugural summit was held in Washington in December 2025
questions.e: Pax Silica brings together technology and resource partners such as Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the Netherlands, the UK, Israel, the UAE and Australia to secure supply chains for chips, AI and critical minerals. It is different from the India-led IPOI, which is a maritime arrangement.

questions.q:
India welcomed Spain joining the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. IPOI is a treaty-based arrangement concluded under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
2. It was launched by India in November 2019 at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok.
3. It is organised around seven pillars, including maritime security, maritime ecology and disaster risk reduction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IPOI is a voluntary, non-treaty arrangement, so 1 is wrong; it works through pillars led by partner countries (for example, maritime security is co-led by India and the UK). 2026 is also the India-Spain Dual Year of Culture, Tourism and AI, marking 70 years of relations.

questions.q: The United Kingdom defended its agreement on the Chagos archipelago in January 2026. Which one of the following is correct?
o: The UK will transfer sovereignty to Seychelles and close the Diego Garcia base entirely
The UK will transfer sovereignty to Mauritius, following a binding 2019 ITLOS judgment on maritime boundaries
The UK will transfer sovereignty to Mauritius while retaining a 99-year lease on the Diego Garcia base, following a 2019 ICJ advisory opinion that the 1965 detachment of Chagos was unlawful
The UK will transfer sovereignty to Mauritius and hand the Diego Garcia base to the United States on a permanent basis
questions.e: The ICJ's 2019 opinion was advisory, not a binding judgment, and it was the International Court of Justice, not ITLOS, that found the 1965 separation from Mauritius unlawful. The deal keeps the strategic Diego Garcia base through a lease, and it drew criticism from US President Trump.

questions.q:
The UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) released a report titled 'We lost everything - even hope for justice' on Sri Lanka. Consider the following statements:
1. It documents conflict-related sexual violence mainly by state security forces against Tamil civilians during the civil war.
2. It urges acknowledgement, a formal apology and an independent prosecution mechanism.
3. The Sri Lankan civil war ended in 2009, and the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and Ranasinghe Premadasa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1987 Accord was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and Sri Lankan President J.R. Jayewardene, not Premadasa, who succeeded him in 1989. The civil war ended in May 2009, and the report calls for accountability for the abuses.

questions.q:
US President Donald Trump announced a 25% tariff on any country doing business with Iran. Consider the following statements:
1. India's analysts assessed the direct impact on India as minimal.
2. India-Iran trade rose to nearly USD 15 billion in FY2025 from USD 1.6 billion before 2020.
3. India has a 10-year operating contract for Chabahar Port.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The trade figures are reversed: India-Iran trade fell from nearly USD 15 billion before 2020 to USD 1.6 billion in FY2025, which is why the tariff matters little directly. India's Chabahar contract (10 years) is the strategic stake, while China bought over 80% of Iran's shipped oil in 2025.

questions.q: The 6th ASEAN-India Digital Ministers' Meeting in January 2026 was co-chaired virtually by India and an ASEAN member. Which one of the following correctly identifies the co-chair and a key outcome?
o: Vietnam; operationalisation of the ASEAN-India Fund for Digital Future
Indonesia; operationalisation of the ASEAN-India Fund for Digital Future
Vietnam; operationalisation of the ASEAN-India Science and Technology Development Fund
Singapore; adoption of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement
questions.e: The meeting took the theme 'Adaptive ASEAN: From Connectivity to Connected Intelligence', reviewed the 2025 ASEAN-India Digital Work Plan and welcomed a 2026 plan. 2026 is also the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation.

questions.q:
India introduced an e-Production Investment Business Visa (e-B-4) for Chinese nationals in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The visa is applied for fully online through the Bureau of Immigration's e-Visa portal.
2. Inviting companies must register on DPIIT's National Single Window System.
3. It allows stays of up to two years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The visa allows stays of up to six months, not two years, and is processed in about 45-50 days. It is one of the people-centric measures agreed to reset India-China ties.

questions.q:
The Indian Navy's First Training Squadron called at Phuket (Thailand) and Belawan (Indonesia) in January 2026 under the MAHASAGAR vision. Consider the following statements:
1. India is due to take over the chair of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) from Thailand in February 2026.
2. IONS was conceived by the Indian Navy in 2008.
3. The inaugural IONS was held in Mumbai in 2008.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The inaugural IONS edition was held in New Delhi in February 2008, not Mumbai. The squadron comprised INS Tir, INS Shardul, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi, reflecting India's naval diplomacy in the Indian Ocean.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026 and became the 21st member of the eurozone.
Statement-II: Sweden and Poland are among the European Union members that have already adopted the euro.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Bulgaria replaced the lev and followed Croatia, the 20th member in 2023. Sweden, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania and Denmark remain outside the eurozone, so Statement-II is incorrect. The euro itself launched on 1 January 1999 with 11 countries.

questions.q: Five countries began two-year terms as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council on 1 January 2026. Which one of the following was NOT among them?
questions.e: The new members elected by the General Assembly in June 2025 were Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia and Liberia. Pakistan is a continuing member whose two-year term runs through 2026. The Council has five permanent and ten non-permanent members.
questions.s: UN Office in Haiti; UNSC election 2025

questions.q:
On 3 January 2026 the United States struck Caracas and captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Consider the following statements:
1. Maduro and his wife were flown to New York to face narco-terrorism charges.
2. After the operation, the Venezuelan Supreme Court ordered the Speaker of the National Assembly to act as interim president.
3. The UN Security Council held an emergency meeting on 5 January.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court instead ordered Vice President Delcy Rodriguez to serve as interim president. The operation, called Operation Absolute Resolve, was justified by a 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine (1823), which opposed European intervention in the Americas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about US actions in January 2026:
1. A US presidential memorandum directed withdrawal from 66 international organisations, including 31 UN entities.
2. The US withdrawal from the World Health Organization took effect on 22 January 2026.
3. The US is a founding member of the International Solar Alliance, which it has now been directed to leave.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The International Solar Alliance was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015, and the US joined only in 2021, so 3 is wrong. The ISA is headquartered in Gurugram, and the withdrawal list also covers bodies such as the IPCC and UN DESA.
questions.s: All India Radio News, 7 Jan 2026; GMA Network, 22 Jan 2026

questions.q: Adani Group started construction of the 570 MW Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in January 2026. Which one of the following is correct?
o: It is a storage project on the Arun river in Nepal, developed by Adani Power alone
It is a run-of-river project in Bhutan, developed by NHPC and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh
It is a run-of-river project in Chukha district of Bhutan, developed as a joint venture with Druk Green Power Corporation on a build-own-operate-transfer basis
It is a pumped-storage project on the Teesta river in Sikkim
questions.e: Wangchhu (the Wangchu or Raidak river) is in Chukha, Bhutan, with Adani Power holding 49% and Druk Green 51%. Winter power meets Bhutan's own demand and the summer surplus is exported to India. The NHPC and Arunachal Pradesh JV belongs to the Kamala project, not this one.

questions.q:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited India on 12-13 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was his first visit to India as Chancellor, with talks held at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar.
2. Germany expressed its intent to join MILAN, the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium and Tarang Shakti.
3. The visit marked 50 years of diplomatic relations between India and Germany.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The visit marked 25 years of the India-Germany strategic partnership and 75 years of diplomatic relations, not 50. Other outcomes included a roadmap on defence co-development and co-production, visa-free transit through German airports for Indian passport holders, and backing for IMEC.

questions.q:
The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ, or High Seas Treaty) entered into force on 17 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 2023 under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (1982).
2. It entered into force 120 days after the 60th ratification.
3. It allows the first country to extract marine genetic resources from the high seas to keep all the benefits, without benefit sharing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Marine genetic resources and fair benefit sharing is one of the treaty's four pillars, so 3 is wrong; the others are area-based management tools such as marine protected areas, environmental impact assessments, and capacity building and technology transfer. It is the first legally binding treaty to conserve marine biodiversity in international waters.

questions.q:
During the UAE President's visit to New Delhi on 19 January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India and the UAE signed a Letter of Intent toward a Strategic Defence Partnership.
2. HPCL and ADNOC Gas signed a 10-year LNG supply deal of 5 million tonnes per year starting in 2028.
3. The leaders set a target of doubling bilateral trade from USD 100 billion to USD 200 billion by 2032.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The LNG deal covers 0.5 million tonnes per year, ten times less than stated in 2. The trade target builds on the 2022 CEPA, and the leaders also agreed to explore Small Modular Reactors, a 'House of India' in Abu Dhabi and 'Digital Embassies'.
questions.s: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 19 Jan 2026

questions.q:
At the World Economic Forum in Davos on 21 January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. US President Trump announced a 'framework of a future deal' on Greenland and dropped a threatened tariff on eight European countries.
2. Trump said he would use force to acquire Greenland if talks failed.
3. Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Trump said he would not use force to acquire Greenland. Greenland is a self-governing territory of Denmark, which is why the US push drew European tariff threats and renewed debate on Arctic competition, including China's 'Polar Silk Road'.

questions.q:
Trump launched his 'Board of Peace' at the World Economic Forum in Davos on 22 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. Leaders signed its charter at the launch.
2. It was set up for Gaza under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025), with a mandate to 31 December 2027.
3. India attended the launch and joined as a founding member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India was invited but neither accepted nor declined and did not attend the launch, so 3 is wrong; Pakistan's Prime Minister attended, while India, France, the UK, China and Germany were absent. Nickolay Mladenov is High Representative for Gaza.

questions.q:
The UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) marked its 80th anniversary on 23 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It was created by the UN Charter in 1945.
2. It is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations.
3. Its 54 members are elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms.
4. It is headquartered in Geneva.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ECOSOC is headquartered in New York, not Geneva, though it meets in both cities. Statements 1 to 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set the Doomsday Clock to 85 seconds to midnight on 27 January 2026, the closest it has ever been.
Statement-II: The Doomsday Clock was created in 1947 by the Bulletin, which was founded in 1945 at the University of Chicago by Manhattan Project scientists.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The clock moved from 89 seconds in 2025, citing nuclear arsenals, AI and biological threats. Statement-II is true background (the clock began at seven minutes to midnight) but does not explain why the setting moved closer.
questions.s: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, 27 Jan 2026

questions.q:
India and the European Union announced the conclusion of negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement on 27 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The announcement was made in New Delhi, with Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa as chief guests at Republic Day 2026.
2. The EU granted concessions to India on sugar, ethanol and rice.
3. The deal still requires legal scrubbing and ratification by the EU Member States and the European Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The EU made no concessions on sugar, ethanol, rice, soft wheat, beef, poultry, milk powders, bananas or honey, which are sensitive for its farmers. The agreement creates a free trade zone of about 2 billion people but takes effect only after legal scrubbing and ratification.
questions.s: European Commission IP Helpdesk; Drishti IAS, Jan 2026
